description:
## Background

`OctoPi.AI.Message.User.content` is typed `String.t() | [Content.user_block()]`
(see apps/octo_pi_ai/lib/octo_pi/ai/message/user.ex). Same dual shape for
ToolResult.content. The moduledoc on User even calls the binary form a
"shorthand for a single text block." Upstream pi-mono uses the same
`string | (TextContent | ImageContent)[]` shape (packages/ai/src/types.ts
`UserMessage.content`), so we faithfully ported a latent ambiguity.

The cost shows up everywhere downstream because every consumer has to
defensively branch on which shape it got:

  - apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/compaction/tokens.ex
      defp user_chars(c) when is_binary(c), do: byte_size(c)
      defp user_chars(c) when is_list(c), do: ...
      defp tool_result_chars(c) when is_binary(c), ...
      defp tool_result_chars(c) when is_list(c), ...
  - apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/compaction/serialize.ex
      defp user_text(c) when is_binary(c), do: c
      defp user_text(c) when is_list(c), do: ...
      defp tool_result_text/1   (same dual shape)
  - apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/components/tree_selector.ex
      defp extract_content_text(s) when is_binary(s), ...
      defp has_text_content?(s) when is_binary(s), ...
  - apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/session/message_writer.ex
      defp user_content(text) when is_binary(text), ...
  - apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex
      defp message_text(%{content: c}) when is_binary(c), do: c
      defp message_text(%{content: c}) when is_list(c), do: ...

This was the source of opi-tze.6 (dequeue overlay crash on list-content)
and shaped the pragmatic-but-redundant message_text/1 helper added in
opi-tze.3. Every new consumer that forgets to handle one of the two
shapes is a latent crash.

The persistence layer is already clean: MessageReader.content_blocks/1
lifts string content into `[%Text{text: ...}]` unconditionally on read
(apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/session/message_reader.ex L70).
So inside the agent's transcript after a session reload, content is
already list-shape. The string-shape only enters the system through
two doors: `Message.normalize/1` (when given a binary) and direct
struct construction (mostly tests).

## Plan: Option A — canonicalize at construction

1. Tighten `Message.normalize/1` so any User.t() / ToolResult.t() it
   returns has list-shape content. Binaries become
   `[%OctoPi.AI.Content.Text{text: <bin>}]`. User structs already
   carrying string content get lifted.
2. Tighten the type contracts on `OctoPi.AI.Message.User.t()` and
   `OctoPi.AI.Message.ToolResult.t()` to drop the binary alternative.
   The "shorthand" comment on the moduledoc goes away.
3. Plug the back-door: `OctoPi.Agent.set_messages/2` currently does
   NOT route through `Message.normalize/1`. Add normalization there.
4. Drop dual-shape branches in every downstream consumer (tokens,
   serialize, tree_selector, message_writer, interactive,
   anthropic/openai request builders if applicable).
5. Update tests that build `%User{content: "..."}` directly to either
   build list-shape or route through `Message.normalize/1`.
6. Touch-ups picked up from opi-tze post-review:
   a. Consolidate `decide_next(_terminal_reason, ...)` into a shared
      drain helper (currently duplicates `drain_steering_into_messages`
      logic inline).
   b. DRY the three `start_coder_session_for_*!` helpers in
      apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/interactive_test.exs.
   c. Use `Components.Input.set_value/2` in `restore_queued_to_editor`
      so cursor clamping etc. goes through the canonical path.

## Acceptance

- `OctoPi.AI.Message.User.t()` and `OctoPi.AI.Message.ToolResult.t()`
  have list-only `content` types.
- No `is_binary(content)` clause remains on the User/ToolResult
  consumer side (provider-specific request builders may keep their
  own dual-handling for backward-compat with persisted JSON).
- All apps' tests pass; the probe at .pi/tmp/queue-test/probe_queue.exs
  still passes 8/8.
- The session-on-disk format is unchanged (writers still emit string
  shorthand when they wish; readers still lift on entry).

## Sub-tickets break the work into reviewable slices.
title: [EPIC] Canonicalize User/ToolResult content to list-shape at construction
